basis: Every evidence command re-runs and produces the stated output, so I re-derived the claim independently and it splits in two. (A) The Go package IS externally unreachable, and I established this by a stronger route than the finding used: `git grep -n 'slabledger/internal/platform/cache' -- '*.go'` returns exactly ONE line tree-wide, internal/integration/pricing_test.go:12, and that file carries `//go:build integration` (line 4). One importer, integration-gated, settles external reachability for the whole package at once rather than symbol-by-symbol. No dot-import, no alias, no second importer; cmd/slabledger and cmd/psa-harvest both import nothing from it. (B) The rest of the cluster is LIVE, and the finding is affirmatively wrong about it. Dockerfile.harvest:39 is `ENTRYPOINT ["/app/psa-harvest", "--cache", "/tmp/psa-harvest-cache.json"]` — the deployed harvest container passes the flag on every start. The consumption chain is closed and entirely in-repo: cmd/psa-harvest/main.go:39 hands os.Args[1:] to parseBaselineFlag, which by construction passes `-cache` through untouched (cmd/psa-harvest/baseline_test.go:51,53 assert exactly that passthrough, in a default-build test); main.go:49 calls config.Load(args); loader.go:239 builds the FlagSet with `flag.ContinueOnError` and loader.go:262 returns fs.Parse's error; Load propagates it (loader.go:21-24); run() wraps it and main.go:44 calls log.Fatalf. Delete the `-cache` registration at loader.go:253 and that container dies at startup with `flag provided but not defined: -cache`. The mkdir is live for the same reason: Dockerfile.harvest:34-38 documents that EnsureDirectories runs in production and that the default `data/cache.json` would mkdir under the read-only /app WORKDIR and fail — the flag exists specifically to steer that mkdir to a writable path. Four of the five members named in the finding's own title (Config.Cache.Path, the -cache flag, its validation, EnsureDirectories' mkdir) are therefore live production surface.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: The root cause is the declared searched_universe: 'git-tracked *.go files'. A CLI flag's consumers are not Go source — they are Dockerfiles, compose files, and entrypoints — so the search was structurally incapable of seeing the one live consumer, and no amount of Go-side grepping would have surfaced it. Three consequences. (1) The title, subject identity, and severity assert a five-member dead cluster when only one member is dead; the finding navigated LENS-BRIEF trap 1 correctly on the Go side and then missed a live caller sitting outside the file glob. (2) proposed_fix instructs removal of 'the -cache CLI flag registration in loader.go' and 'EnsureDirectories'. Executed as written at mechanical tier — the tier that authorizes unqualified deletion — that breaks the deployed psa-harvest container. (3) acceptance_criteria #2 ('grep for ... \'-cache\' flag across the repo returns no remaining references') is unachievable and actively misleading: it would drive a fixer to strip Dockerfile.harvest:39 and the cmd/psa-harvest/baseline_test.go:51,53 fixtures, neither of which appears in blast_radius. A fixer working from the acceptance criteria alone cannot prove this fix correct, so it is not ticketable as written. Minor, separate: proposed_fix enumerates the package as 'cache.go, cache_test.go, cache_bench_test.go' and omits file_store.go and lru.go (blast_radius's `internal/platform/cache/*` does cover them).
